title: yay Liberation, justice for Whitney White. We will get you that Tony!...
transcript: Liberation winning the Tony Award for best play last night is so incredibly important. And as Bess Wohl stated, this is the first time in nearly 40 years that an American woman has won the award. I have seen that statistic be a little bit misinterpreted because a woman has won since Wendy Wasserstein won for Heidi Chronicles in 1989. Yasmina Reza won for both art in 1998 and god of carnage in 2009. However, she is a French woman, so Thus the American part of that is an important aspect. In my opinion. The more harrowing statistic is that in the 79 years of the Tony Awards, only five plays written by women have ever won. Two of those written by Yasmina Reza, and one of them was written by Frances Goodrich, who co wrote the play The Diary of Anne Frank with her husband. If you look out at all of the nominees, it's only about 10% of the nominees have ever been written by women, which again, just a harrowing statistic. I am so happy that Liberation won. I really hope that we don't have to wait over a decade for the next female playwright to win a Tony Award. Also, as a historical side note, 1998 was actually a huge year for women because not only did Yasmina Reza win best play, you also had Lynn Ahrens win best original score. She was only the second woman to ever win the award for co-Writing ragtime with Steven Flaherty. Following Betty Comden's three wins throughout her career, it wasn't until 2013 that we got the first woman to win best original score for a score that she wrote by herself, with Cyndi Lauper winning for Kinky Boots. 2015 was when we got the first female duo with Lisa Kron and Janine Tesori writing Fun Home. But 1998 was also the first year that a woman ever won for best director of either category. But it happened to just be both categories that year, with both Julie Taymor winning for The Lion King and Garry Hynes winning for The Beauty Queen of Leenane. I have so many thoughts on genders and class and opportunities and how they are doled out in this industry in general, but that's a much larger conversation. All this to say go see theatre at your off Broadway theatres and regional houses that are highlighting and platforming female writers and directors because there's so many fantastic ones. So many of the shows that I've seen in the last couple weeks, even outside of New York, especially outside of New York, have been by female writers and directors who have never been on Broadway in those capacities before. I cannot recommend supporting it enough. It's some of my favourite work that I've seen this year.
